tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: According to the Department, income chargeable to tax amounting to Rs 1,36,76,65,149/- (out of which Rs 1,25,80,23,649/- is still under verification by the Department) has escaped assessment within the meaning of Section 147 of the Income-tax Act, 1961. Accordingly, a show cause notice under Section 148A(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 was issued to the Company, seeking an explanation as to why a notice under Section 148 of the Act should not be issued on the basis of the aforementioned information, in accordance with the provisions of Section 148A(3)(ii) of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Office of The Assistant Commissioner Of Income Tax Circle 1(1)(1), Vadodara
tax_litigation.status: The Company submitted its reply to the notice issued under Section 148A on 10 April 2026, along with supporting documents and legal submissions, contending that no income had escaped assessment. After considering the submissions, the Assessing Officer passed an order under Section 148A(d) on 27 June 2026 and issued a notice under Section 148 for AY 2020–21. The Company is required to file its return of income within 90 days from the date of the notice. Thereafter, the reassessment proceedings will continue in accordance with the provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961. As on 30 June 2026, the matter is pending at the stage of filing the return in response to the notice issued under Section 148.

tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner (HQ Preventive) CGST & C. Excise Vadodara-l
tax_litigation.status: Oriental Aromatics Limited (Company) has received a Show Cause cum demand Notice (SCN) from the office of Assistant Commissioner(HQ Preventive) CGST & C. Excise Vadodara-I against GSTN : 24AAACC9211E1Z7 proposing a demand of Rs.95,68,533. The notice alleges that one of the Company's vendors, whose GST registration was suspended, was considered by the Department to be a non-existent supplier based on the findings of its investigation. The SCN covers the period from 1 April 2020 to 31 March 2025. In response to the allegations, the Company has submitted its detailed reply along with supporting documentary evidence to substantiate the genuineness of the transactions undertaken and to address the observations raised by the concerned GST authority. At this stage, the matter is pending adjudication, and the proposed demand of Rs 95,68,533 has not been crystallised into a confirmed financial liability. The last hearing was scheduled for 12 October 2026; however, the Company filed an adjournment request. Accordingly, the Company is awaiting communication of the next hearing date
